assertions: MET. Generation resolves the EXTENDS closure before TLC runs and gives SANY the directories it found as TLA-Library (TLC 2.19 has no -lib flag, and it does not search the current directory -- both verified). The module's own directory wins, then --module-path, then sibling directories holding .tla files, which is what makes specs/case_modules/ -> specs/program_model/ work with no flag; two siblings defining the same module is an error naming both. The view's spec_manifest.yaml is found along the same path, so the declaration, budgets and coverage record still describe one project. Both ex4 modules regenerate in place with cases/actions/declared_view_actions/case_module byte-equal to the committed copy-and-delete evidence. An unresolvable EXTENDS is now one sentence BEFORE the JVM starts, naming the module, every directory searched and --module-path, instead of a SANY AbortException under a fail-closed complexity paragraph. 11 regression tests, one of which pins the shipped ex4 layout.

MET, and one command in it fails on purpose. references/case_modules.md, 'Worked example: an internal-only project', was run verbatim end to end on examples/validation/ex4_pipeline_coherent (internal view, no testgraph, no bindings): enumerate the action set, generate the view corpus (330 cases), generate the slice and the Given in place (50 and 6), validate, aggregate coverage (UNCOVERED: none), and execute the Given's corpus against the project's UNCHANGED adapters with two --import-root ('executed 6 cases in batch'). Step 6 is the slice against the same mapping, which refuses -- that is CM-F5, published as a refusal rather than hidden. Two smaller frictions fixed on the way: --out now says where a relative path landed, and the --import-root error names both roots. Recorded in results/internal-view-worked-example.{sh,txt}.

MET. references/case_modules.md, 'The authoring asymmetry: a slice comes from outside, a Given cannot', states it as a table of what each form requires and where that knowledge lives, and names the split that makes a Given commissionable from outside (the outsider supplies the CLAIM, someone with the model writes the predicate). prompts/aspect_decomposition.md Step 3 says the same at the point of authoring.

MET as LABELLED UNENFORCEABLE, deliberately, inside Step 0 where the requirement is made. Two candidate checks -- require a non-empty Source, reject 'the model'/'derived' -- are named and rejected in the text as guards a determined agent walks around, which this epic has already shipped once. The honest contract replaces them: provenance is an unverified claim, an authorless decomposition must be labelled unreviewed, and a consumer asks the named source directly.

ADJACENT, FIXED: parameter recovery did not follow EXTENDS. Found while running the worked example, not in the brief. A case module declares no actions, so recipes read from its own text alone recovered nothing: the view's corpus carried 330/330 arguments while its two case modules carried 0/50 and 0/6, and the adapters refused those corpora case by case with 'no usable argument for `i`'. Recipes are now built over the whole hierarchy, base modules first -- 50/50 and 6/6, and the Given's corpus executes. Single-file specs are unaffected; examples/distributed_history's committed corpora are now stale with respect to this and were not regenerated.

NEGATIVE: the brief's 'Step 1's jq pipeline assumes JSON-only stdout' did not reproduce -- that command writes 6,703 bytes to stdout and 0 to stderr, and every error path prints to stderr. What did reproduce is fixed: --spec-root does not resolve the positional .tla/.cfg, and Step 1(b) required PyYAML, which this toolchain deliberately does not depend on.

OWNER-AUTHORIZED DELETION: scripts/spec_evolution.py CFG_KEYWORDS and its skip are gone, no reference remains anywhere, and the three model-pair validator tests RP-04 measured as load-bearing on it are green.

ticket.objective: Everything the outside-in eval run hit while trying to use case modules for real. (a) EV-02-DF-02: a case module CANNOT generate from where the docs put it -- TLC runs with cwd = the .tla's directory and no module search path, so a module in specs/case_modules/ cannot EXTENDS a view in specs/program_model/. The agent had to copy the module beside the view, generate, and delete the copy, so the checked-in module is NOT reproducible in place, and the failure surfaces as a 30-line TLC AbortException behind a misleading fail-closed paragraph. (b) EV-02-DF-05: every published command assumes an EXTERNAL view (`--view external`, `generated/testgraph/`, `testgraph_bindings.yml`); an internal-only project has no worked example anywhere, and this is X-P3 failing again. Also fix the smaller friction the run recorded: `--out` resolving against the .tla's directory rather than cwd undocumented, the `--import-root` error naming one root when two are needed, and Step 1's command in the aspect prompt not running as written. (c) EV-02-DF-04, the methodological half: a SLICE is writable from action names alone, but a GIVEN must constrain every variable of the view, so it can only be written from the inside -- the aspect came from outside and the Given could not. Neither doc says so. State the limit, and make Step 0's author-provenance requirement either checkable or honestly labelled unenforceable (an eval agent produced a schema-valid, coverage-clean decomposition with no author in the loop and had to flag its own violation).
